anomalies.observed: In mcu.kicad_sch the heater connector J6 (Screw_Terminal_01x02) pin 2 is wired up to U6's IN pin (pin 1, left side of the TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1 symbol), while the green 'HEATER' label coming from U1 GPIO1 (pin 13) attaches to U6's right-hand (output/DIAG_EN) side. The switch's input and its output are therefore interchanged relative to the specification.
anomalies.expected: Spec: '`IN`/`DIAG_EN` (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net /Microcontroller/HEATER)' and '`OUT` (pin 7) feeds the heater connector `J6` pin 2.'

evidence.quote: `IN`/`DIAG_EN` (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net `/Microcontroller/HEATER`), `OUT` (pin 7) feeds the heater connector `J6` pin 2

Sheet /Microcontroller/ (mcu.kicad_sch): U6 TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1 — wire from J6 pin 2 rises to U6 pin 1 (IN); green 'HEATER' label fed from U1 pin 13 GPIO1/ADC1_CH1/XTAL_32K_N attaches to U6's output-side pins

anomalies.impact: The high-side switch can never be turned on by firmware: its IN pin sits at the heater-element node (near ground), so GPIO1's bang-bang control only drives the switch's OUT pin. The oven never receives heater power even though D2 (heater LED) still follows GPIO1, i.e. a silent loss of the board's primary function.

anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet (power.kicad_sch) the two 4-pin fan headers J7/J8 are tapped from one vertical bus that starts at the '+12V' power symbol at the top and continues down to the 'GND' symbol at the bottom; both pin 1 and pin 2 of each header are connected to this same bus.
anomalies.expected: Spec: the +12V net of the barrel jack '(J7/J8 pin 2)' only — i.e. pin 2 of each header is the 12 V pin and pin 1 is the fan ground return (standard 4-pin fan pinout: 1=GND, 2=+12V, 3=TACH, 4=PWM/NC).

evidence.quote: Also on this net: `U5` pin 7/7_1 (`IN1`), `D7` (plain diode, `Device:D`), bulk caps `C1` ... and `C2`, and the two fan-header 12 V pins (`J7`/`J8` pin 2).
Sheet /Power/ (power.kicad_sch): +12V symbol above J7 with a vertical wire that taps J7 pin 1, J7 pin 2, J8 pin 1, J8 pin 2 and terminates at the GND symbol below J8

anomalies.impact: Pin 1 of each fan header (normally the fan's ground return) is placed on the +12V net, and the +12V rail is bridged to GND through the same bus — a supply short that prevents the 12 V input from powering the board at all; if not shorted, the fans would see 0 V across their supply pins and never run (firmware would raise a fan-stall run fault).

parsed.summary: The drawing deviates from the specified design in the heater-switch wiring: U6's IN pin (1) is wired to the heater connector J6 instead of being driven by the GPIO1 HEATER net, while the HEATER net lands on the switch's output side, so the heater can never be turned on. A second, lower-confidence issue is the fan-header wiring, where J7/J8 pin 1 appears tied to the same +12V bus that runs to GND.
